mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the tightening signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the labor market weakening signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or the correlation between GDP declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production by more than 1% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive supply signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and a decrease in retail sales signal a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, which may indicate a temporary reduction in corporate earnings from retail sectors, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases and RSAFS decreases simultaneously
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect between HOUST and RSAFS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases simultaneously
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect between PAYEMS and UNRATE on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index over three consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which erodes real earnings and increases borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of periods with rising CPI, or the correlation between CPI increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in retail sales combined with a rise in the unemployment rate signals a weakening consumer demand environment, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases and UNRATE increases simultaneously
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect between RSAFS and UNRATE on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
